body.statement: The envelopes satisfy \(\mathcal C_P=\{u\in C(X_0):\operatorname{Lip}(u)\le L,\ \ell_P\le u\le r_P\}\), and \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\) if and only if \(\ell_P(x)\le r_P(x)\) for every \(x\in X_0\).
body.justification: The result converts latent-model compatibility into an observable necessary-and-sufficient envelope test.
body.gap: Existing conditional-moment methods provide general tests, but no exact obstacle certificate for these coupled baseline-specific cones.
body.consumer: Researchers can distinguish rejection of the maintained bounded-trend model from mere failure of point identification.
body.proof_tex:
For \((d,z)\in H\), the functions of \(x\)
\[
g(d,z)-K|z|-L|x-d|
\quad\text{and}\quad
g(d,z)+K|z|+L|x-d|
\]
are \(L\)-Lipschitz.  Suprema, infima, maxima, and minima of finite-valued functions sharing the same Lipschitz constant retain that constant.  Compactness of \(H\) and continuity of \(g\) make all displayed envelopes finite.  Thus \(\ell_P\) and \(r_P\) are continuous and \(L\)-Lipschitz.

If \(u\in\mathcal C_P\), then for every \((d,z)\in H\) and \(x\in X_0\),
\[
u(x)\geq u(d)-L|x-d|
\geq g(d,z)-K|z|-L|x-d|,
\]
and \(u(x)\geq-M\).  Taking the supremum and maximum proves \(u\geq\ell_P\).  Similarly,
\[
u(x)\leq u(d)+L|x-d|
\leq g(d,z)+K|z|+L|x-d|,
\]
together with \(u(x)\leq M\), proves \(u\leq r_P\).

Conversely, suppose \(u\) is continuous, \(\operatorname{Lip}(u)\leq L\), and \(\ell_P\leq u\leq r_P\).  The definitions give \(\ell_P\geq-M\) and \(r_P\leq M\), so \(\|u\|_\infty\leq M\).  At each \((d,z)\in H\),
\[
\ell_P(d)\geq g(d,z)-K|z|,
\qquad
r_P(d)\leq g(d,z)+K|z|.
\]
Therefore
\[
g(d,z)-K|z|\leq u(d)\leq g(d,z)+K|z|,
\]
which is exactly the observed cone restriction.  This proves
\[
\mathcal C_P
=\{u\in C(X_0):\operatorname{Lip}(u)\leq L, \ell_P\leq u\leq r_P\}.
\]

Nonemptiness plainly implies \(\ell_P\leq r_P\).  Conversely, if \(\ell_P\leq r_P\), take \(u=\ell_P\).  It is \(L\)-Lipschitz, satisfies \(\ell_P\leq u\leq r_P\), and hence belongs to \(\mathcal C_P\) by the characterization just proved.  Thus the pointwise envelope inequality is also sufficient.
